thread:
emma: quick q — noticed a few production pods stuck during spot eviction + karpenter consolidation. PDB seems to be preventing evictions so fallback on on-demand is delayed. anyone run into this pattern? linked a repro in PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1234

matt: if your PDB is minAvailable: replicas it will block every eviction. switch to maxUnavailable (number or %) for non-critical replicas. also check podAntiAffinity so replicas spread across nodes. :thinking_face:

julia: we solved similar by using two provisioners: one spot-preferred and one on-demand-for-fallback with a taint on on-demand nodes and a toleration for critical pods. terraform snippet we used (trimmed):
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_manifest" "karpenter_provisioner_on_demand" {
  manifest = {
    apiVersion = "karpenter.sh/v1alpha5"
    kind = "Provisioner"
    metadata = { name = "on-demand-fallback" }
    spec = {
      requirements = [ { key = "node.kubernetes.io/instance-type", operator = "In", values = ["c6i.large"] } ]
      taints = [ { key = "preemptible", value = "false", effect = "NoSchedule" } ]
      ttlSecondsUntilExpired = 259200
    }
  }
}
```

ryan: regarding PDB, for deployments i prefer `maxUnavailable: "25%"` so an eviction can proceed during scale events. for statefulsets you might need `podManagementPolicy: Parallel` if you want fast moves. example PDB manifest: 
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: web-pdb
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
```

emma: good tips. question on secrets: our node bootstrap script pulls a Vault token from instance profile and writes a kube secret for the node-provisioner sidecar. i worry about race where pod schedules before secret exists. any patterns?

sam: race is common. options: make the provisioner create secrets via controller (infra-agent), or use an initContainer that waits for secret + tolerate taints so it won't land on new node until ready. also bump `gracePeriodSeconds` and `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` where applicable, and set `evictionTimeout` in the kubelet config if you control nodes.

emma: thanks — so actionable: 1) change PDB to maxUnavailable 25% for web deployments, 2) add taint "preemptible=true:NoSchedule" to spot provisioner and toleration on critical pods, 3) add on-demand provisioner with taint false as in julia's snippet, 4) adjust bootstrap to create secret before marking node ready (or use toleration+initContainer). i'll open a PR with the PDB + toleration changes.
